name: Wali Deccani
bio: Wali of the Deccan is called in the book the first to write an Urdu diwan and the Father of Urdu poetry; born at Aurungabad, he wrote in the latter half of the seventeenth century, held a just balance between Sunnis and Shiahs, and did not flatter any ruler in his verses.

The one piece given here is drawn from Hindustani Lyrics (London: The Sufi Publishing Society, 1919), in the English verse of Inayat Khan and Jessie Duncan Westbrook. It is a free rendering, not a literal translation, and the original Urdu poem is untitled; it is named here by its first line.

poems.title: O Lovely One, when to the ravished sight
poems.author: Wali Deccani
poems.translator: trans. Inayat Khan and Jessie Duncan Westbrook (1919)
poems.text:
O Lovely One, when to the ravished sight
Thou wilt unveil that radiant face of thine,
Each atom of the worlds, catching thy light,
Reflecting thee, bright as a sun shall shine.

Walk not, my flower, within the garden close,
Lest thou should give the bulbul new distress;
For at thy glance each blossom turns a rose
To lure him with her cruel loveliness.

Victorious One, thou hast unsheathed thy sword,
The scimitar of thy beauty gleams again,
So over all thy lovers thou art Lord,
Holding dominion in the hearts of men.

Art thou serene and calm and unafraid
When thou considerest thy tyranny?
Think of the reckoning that shall be made
Between thy heart and mine at Judgment Day.
